evidence: arXiv:2610.00440v1 Remark 6.3 proves attainability for \(M\le d\), \(M\ge d^n\), and certain \(M=d^r\) maximum-distance-separable constructions, but does not state the remaining binary short cases.

At \(n=2\), the remaining \(M=3\) case is attained by \(\{00,01,10\}\). At \(n=3\), the remaining \(M=3,5,6,7\) cases are attained from \(\{000,011,101\}\) and the even-parity four-word core by projection saturation.

Rosati's MDS-based discussion explicitly notes that for binary alphabets only trivial MDS codes of the relevant family exist, so his general lower-bound mechanism does not imply these nonlinear all-message short cases.
